Hey all, short introduction.

I've always wanted to do a Metrocop build. Been a dream build of mine for a few years. I have pored over the various builds. There are eras to the Combine cosplay. Some incredible builds have been posted and they really inspired me to finally commit to one of my own. So, below begins my journey.

Here, I aim to build the most accurate to image look possible. I am basing most of my build on an HD remodeling of the original Metrocop. I am using the model and texture made by mb814 [https://gamebanana.com/skins/141967]. It's higher res and I prefer the look of this one, sans the laceup boots.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/55e461d1f0565-jpg.982243/|55e461d1f0565.jpg|1316|767]]

More to come!

Edit:

By popular demand, the vest template, digitized [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DWIzSIhPVoEUIBlLZ2qZyTu38QpTCS7x/view?usp=sharing]

If you have a better way of making this vest, please PLEASE post about it here! This outfit is constantly evolving.

TL;DR:

The Helmet

Because my goal was absolute accuracy, I needed to make the helmet as close to scale as possible. I took the high res model by mb214 and decided to print it. I figured the whole helmet would be too large for my Ender 3, so I cut it in half.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/48qvadj-jpg.982727/|48QvaDj.jpg|2048|1536]]

Hmm, not great. I printed a bust to see the whole thing.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/relhmxa-jpg.982728/|RElhmxa.jpg|2048|1536]]

Yikes, that is not great. Too low poly, I needed to smooth this model.

The only software I know how to use is Sketchup, so I was basically impotent in this matter. I tried the 3D builder that's built into Windows nowadays to see if I could smooth in there, but no luck. So, I paid a Venezuelan girl on Fiverr $17 to do it. It turned out great.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/rwbjfyt-jpg.982729/|RWBjFYT.jpg|1536|2048]]

I will likely print another one in the future when I learn how, but I wanted something quick. This will serve my needs as a prototype. Also, I printed it too narrow to wear. I hope to convert it into a vacuum forming buck.

Till next time

Funny you should mention that! I have some ideas regarding the vest, so i think the only stitching will be on the jacket and the pants.

The Vest

The first thing I did was a sketch of the vest, as seen above. This helped me think about the construction of it even deeper than I had been visualizing. I wanted to mimic the appearance of the game, I did not have to adhere to the in-game construction. I had been thinking for a while that building each block of the vest out of foam, then joining them together would be superior to just sewing over batting. The vest looks more like armor than it does a pillow.

I got to experimenting.

I started with the center.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/vaebwwm-jpg.983267/|VAebwwm.jpg|2048|1536]]

I used short pieces of cloth to join the cores in the back.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/jmbvyux-jpg.983268/|JmbVYux.jpg|2048|1536]]

Then a quick mockup.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/jnmc04y-jpg.983269/|jnMC04Y.jpg|2048|1536]]

Hmm, no. That won't do. Too flat and weird.

More updates soon.

That's as much as I'll show you, though. I don't think anyone would come back after seeing the monstrosity the prototype was. Not to worry, however. Things are coming together, albeit slowly. For the pants, I am planning a regular fitting, flat fronted pant, preferably in a twill or cotton.

Oh man. I just found some pictures I haven't been able to find before. HL: Alyx reference pics. They changed the Metrocop a bit. I am not sure exactly how I feel about them but I don't think it's bad.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/4rx6vjw-jpg.1295875/|4rX6vjw.jpg|360|652]]

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/xvmjwza-jpg.1295876/|XVmjwza.jpg|453|1200]]

Honestly, I think it simplifies the whole thing a bit. Unfortunately, it makes the boots I just got a little bit obsolete. The new boots fit more like riding boots than jackboots, as I have. Riding boots ain't cheap...

It looks like the vest is now smaller— while maintaining true to the original design— and the jacket is more approachable. In HL:2, it was clearly a vest, as shown in this pic I took off msleeper's blog.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/6p38msk-jpg.1295877/|6P38mSK.jpg|640|360]]

Incorporating the details like the white shoulders and reflective chest square into the jacket will be a bigger job, however. I had made plans regarding the vest, so I am leaning towards the original design. I will perhaps make both, as I intend to make a new vest anyway. The new jacket looks like a black field jacket with white strips going over the shoulder.

The good news is there is likely a commercially available jacket that can be easily modified to resemble the new Metrocop. The bad news is it is probably expensive and will be difficult (read: time) to find cheap. I still continue to do everything for as cheap as I can, after all.

In the end, I think I'm going to combine (heh) all the details from all the renderings I've seen while trying to maintain as true to the original game as I can. As I stated in the beginning, I am basing it largely off the model from mb814. Besides, the old and new are hardly different! The layman will probably call it a stormtrooper, anyway.

Please give me your ideas! I need them.

posts.author: Utri
posts.text:
[Quoted reply omitted; see original post.]

Max Aristov [https://www.artstation.com/maxaristov/prints] is the artist who designed the new metrocops. I sent him a message about them just now. His original designs had a lot more blue, but looked largely the same. Other differences than the ones you noted include a smaller, more streamlined vest. The new one omits rib and shoulder panels in favor of wide straps. The chest reflector is now part of the vest.

The gloves now have buckles. What looked like a shine accent on the original model is now a white stripe on the gloves. What were previously white stripes on the old 'cops shoulders are now zippers. The new boots are better fitting and resemble riding boots. They now have a zipper on the interior of each leg. They now have a white stripe on the outward face of each leg. Overall, the design is hardly touched, the biggest change being the vest. The mask and overall look have survived any alterations. I love it.

Edit: Although, after I think about it, the cutout from the chest of the new vest is a little odd, and I don't think I'll do that. That is like, the most vital spot on the chest, and it's left completely unprotected. Metrocops are unmodified humans, so it's not like their heart was moved. They just might be saved from a lung shot.

Edit 2: Although, lore-wise, this does take place before HL2, so maybe the combine hadn't quite figured out the best way to arm their soldiers. Hence, the different soldiers faced throughout the game.

I'm running in circles....

posts.text:
Alright, so I think it's about time I work out the financing of this project, and maybe budget from there.

The vest has cost a total of: $8

Harbor Freight Foam Mat Set of 4: $8

Blue cotton blend: free from grandma

The mask has cost a total of: $23

Fiverr contract: $17

Plastic: $6

3D Printer: Thanks Santa

The rest will add up to around: $244.74

5 Yards 50mm 2" Satin Ribbon: $1.07

Knee High Boots (mk1): $56.67

Gloves: $32

Jacket: $32

Pants: $20

Belts: $8

Belt Boxes (printed): $6

Belt Box Electronics: $8

And that covers commercially available items I can buy. It will be cheaper to buy any of the above than to make myself (sans the 3D prints, of course. Only in that I have a printer, or else it would once again be cheaper to buy prints than to try to make myself).

That makes for a grand total of $275.74.

Now, that is a fat chunk of change. I could cut it down by buying second hand. I am a big time thrifter and would love to do that, but with the current situation, that is simply not feasible. Unfortunately, I don't think it's something I can deem worthy of pursuing financially at this time. I just lost my job due to COVID and am graduating in a week. It is a tumultuous time, you see. I must eat.

So, I think that will postpone the actual realization of this costume for many months. However, there is still the prototyping I need to do as far as the mask, helmet, and belt boxes. I am also working on a stun-stick, I'll post about it soon.

I want very badly to complete this outfit, but I refuse to give in to half-measures. I have done it before on an iconic character (Boba Fett— yeah, embarassing) and it looks like a cartoon costume. If I cannot do the original design justice, I will not do it at all.

lol guess I psyched myself out a bit there

posts.author: Utri
posts.text:
Bowye [https://www.therpf.com/forums/members/228873/] appreciate your kind words, still a WIP!

I do agree about the efficiency, worked out the whole vest in a day or two.

As for working out the templates, sketching the vest from different angles helped to really lock in a mental model. Used the center square as a reference point, then just sorta eyeballed it from there. It got away from me a bit, as pointed out by another user, but it’s good enough for me.

But, for the most part, it was just cutting out the foam, gluing the backs together with strips of cloth, then trying it on. If it didn’t fit, I trimmed. If it did, move on to heat gun and forming.

When that turned out well, I disassembled and glued batting to the front of the foam and wrapped in cloth, then glued the backs together again.

Hope this helps

Howdy folks,

Priming a post that is coming soon with all my updates to this project. Started learning a bit of Fusion360 and am having a blast redoing my models.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/beltbox-inside-png.1994573/|beltbox inside.PNG|1013|692]]

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/beltbox1-png.1994574/|beltbox1.PNG|955|708]]

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/beltbox2-png.1994575/|beltbox2.PNG|876|780]]

The belt boxes are focused on functionality. Make of that what you will, I'll show off all the printed progress in the next post.

Watching the YouTuber Will Cogley got me interested in designing with assembly in mind, so these files are intended to be easy to print while hiding as many witness marks as possible.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/filter1-png.1994576/|filter1.PNG|892|703]]

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/filter2-png.1994577/|filter2.PNG|908|723]]

I'm still working on my own version of the mask and helmet, but in the meantime worked up some functional filters that you can actually breathe through! Excellent for walking the convention floor, a lot less stuffy.

[[IMAGE:https://www.therpf.com/forums/attachments/stunstick-png.1994578/|stunstick.PNG|1344|805]]

And finally an updated stunstick. I love how this print turned out. Super easy assembly and it paints incredibly well. I based this one off Pixelitz HL2 HD stunstick remake.

I'm printing everything on my Bambu P1S, so YMMV if you decide to print these files. Though these days, most printers seem to be on a pretty similar level of clarity and reliability. If you're still on an Ender 3 (I certainly would NOT know anything about that, nope, not me :p) I commend you for your resilience. Mine has become quite the dust collector, but still a very serviceable machine.

That's all for this short update for now, more to come soon. Guess I just can't stop with this project!
